transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump has praised the arrests of five men Sunday in England in connection with
what British authorities are describing as a suspected terror plot.
They were arrested near a British airbase the U.S. has been using to launch attacks
on Iran.
NPR's Lauren Freire reports from London.
The British government declined to join the U.S. in Israeli war on Iran, but it's allowed
the U.S. to use British airbases for what it calls defensive attacks on Iran.
And Royal Air Force Base Fairford is one of those, hosting American bombers and reconnaissance
aircraft.
Last summer, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said any base used against Iran is a "legitimate
target."
Early Sunday, police say they intercepted three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford and arrested
five suspects.
They have not identified the men who remain in custody on suspicion, police say, of committing
offenses under the Explosives Act and also of preparing a terrorist act.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, London.
For the second year in a row, President Trump is refusing to send hundreds of millions of
dollars to the places that Congress says it has to go.
The move is called a pocket rescission.
The federal government's nonpartisan watchdog Government Accountability Office says the maneuver
is illegal.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
Each year, Congress passes laws which allocate money to the federal government's various
programs and agencies.
That is their constitutional responsibility, the power of the purse.
Now the executive branch is unilaterally withholding money owed to programs the president opposes.
That's $560 million to programs that provide services to refugees and other immigrants,
according to a memo from the White House.
Also $15 million to a Justice Department team tasked with preventing and resolving racial
tensions.
$70 million to programs providing grants and fellowships to support institutions, bringing
foreign students and faculty to the U.S. and tens of millions more to initiatives that
touch on climate change or racial and gender minority work.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
With the critical midterm elections now just over a month away, some Democrats are focusing
on faith as an issue that just might sway voters to their side.
NPR's Jason Derose reports that a noteworthy number of Democratic candidates are members
of clergy.
In Texas, Baptist pastor Frederick Haines is running for an open U.S. House seat in
the Dallas area, and Presbyterian seminary student James Talarico is the Democratic nominee
for Senate there.
A Methodist pastor is the Democratic Senate nominee in Kansas, and a Lutheran pastor and
a Presbyterian chaplain are running as Democrats for two different U.S. House seats in Iowa.
Pew Research has found that fewer than one third of Democrats say religion is important
to them, but communities vary widely, and these candidates appear to be gaining traction.
The Cook Political Report has moved the Texas Senate seat and one Iowa House district from
Lean's Republican to toss-up.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
And this is NPR News.
Two giant pandas from China have arrived at the Atlanta Zoo from member station WABE in
Atlanta.
Alex Helmic reports that the animals were promised by Chinese President Xi Jinping during a state
visit with President Trump last Thursday.
Jinping and Fu Shuang are on loan to Zoo Atlanta for 10 years.
The deal was one of the few firmed outcomes from the three-day visit, with Xi saying it
was a sign of friendship between the two countries.
China has long used pandas as part of its diplomacy.
The last pandas at the zoo were sent back to China in 2024, when a previous deal expired.
The bears will be quarantined for about a month in the zoo's new giant panda complex,
and an opening date for that has not yet been announced.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Helmic in Atlanta.
A strike by musicians at the Cleveland Orchestra has ended.
The musicians agreed Sunday to a new three-year contract.
The deal includes what the musicians say is a fair pay and benefits package, along with
the voice in auditions and improved safety for musicians.
The strike began on Friday, and there was concern that it would jeopardize a planned
European tour, which is now going ahead.
Seven years after becoming the second-highest-grossing film ever, Avengers Endgame had an encore showing
this weekend in movie theaters, and it did not disappoint, grossing $26 million in North
American theaters and landing in first place.
It added another $60 million in overseas sales.
Zack Craiger's reboot of Resident Evil was in second, bringing in $23.3 million, and
the Brad Pitt-led Heart of the Beast landed in third, with $20 million in sales.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Five men arrested in England near RAF Fairford in connection with suspected terror plot
President Trump withholds $560 million in refugee and immigrant services funding from Congress-approved programs
Democratic candidates who are clergy members gaining traction in midterm elections across multiple states
Giant pandas Jinping and Fu Shuang arrive at Atlanta Zoo on loan from China
Cleveland Orchestra musicians end strike after agreeing to new three-year contract with improved pay
Avengers Endgame re-release grosses $26 million domestically, lands in first place at box office
